title: Synthesis of a three-dimensional π-conjugated framework  via  oxidative cross-linking of a bithienyl-functionalized metal–organic framework
content: Three-dimensional π-conjugated frameworks hold great promise for advanced electronic and structural materials, but their construction via direct sp2 or sp-carbon linkages remains challenging. Herein, we report the synthesis of a robust 3D π-conjugated framework through the direct oxidative cross-linking of a metal–organic framework (MOF). A novel organic ligand having bithienyl groups, a derivative of tetraarylterphenyl dicarboxylic acid (4bttpdc), was synthesized and self-assembled with Zn(ii) ions to form a non-interpenetrated IRMOF-16-type crystal (4btIR16). Subsequent oxidative polymerization via the Scholl reaction using FeCl3 successfully cross-linked the proximate bithienyl groups within the MOF pores. Unlike the highly fragile uncross-linked parent MOF, the resulting cross-linked framework (4btIR16_ox) exhibited significant structural stabilization, which enabled the preservation of micro- and mesoporosity after metal ion exclusion (BET surface area of 146.2 m2 g−1). Furthermore, the 3D π-conjugated framework demonstrated an extended effective π-conjugation length with a broadened absorption spectrum from the ultraviolet to near-infrared region, a more than five-fold increase in mechanical stiffness, and thermally activated electrical conductivity. This bottom-up methodology provides a versatile route for designing rigid, highly porous, and electronically active 3D π-conjugated frameworks.
